title: Contract Retention Lifeboat — Rapid Triage & Save Plays
content:
Purpose:
This is a compact, operational playbook for rapid assessment and short-horizon interventions when a customer surfaces indicators that their upcoming contract may not renew. The goal is to create a fast, repeatable triage flow (0–14 days) that stabilizes the relationship, re-establishes measurable value, and builds a clear path to renewal discussion.

Scope and audience:
- Intended users: CSMs, Solutions Engineers, Customer Success Managers (AMs), Sales AE, and an on-call Renewal Ops partner.
- When to use: triggered by QBR signals, usage drop-off, support escalations, budget messaging from customer, or AE/CS intuition.

High-level principle (LIFEBOAT):
- Listen: get a short-runbook interview with buyer+user stakeholders in <48h.
- Identify: map root cause (cost, quality/regression, product fit, org change, procurement).
- Fast experiments: roll small PV (proof) actions to re-demonstrate value in <10 business days.
- Escalate judiciously: use executive touchpoints only when clear ROI ask exists.
- Backstop offers: calibrated commercial concessions with defined exit conditions.
- Track: measurable outcomes + single source of truth for the play.

Risk signal heatmap (quick scoring):
- Score each customer 0–10 across three axes, then sum (max 30):
  1) Usage delta (last 90d vs baseline) — 0 (flat/growth) to 10 (steep drop)
  2) Health signals (open bugs, infra incidents, eval regressions) — 0–10
  3) Commercial/people signals (budget messages, procurement delays, exec churn) — 0–10
- Triage bands: 0–9 = Green (monitor), 10–18 = Amber (action required in 7–14d), 19–30 = Red (immediate lifeboat; <72h response cadence).

Rapid triage checklist (first 48h):
1) The 20-minute rapid intake call (CS owner + AE + SE optional):
   - Participants: buyer, primary users, procurement contact (if available).
   - Ask: top 3 reasons renewal may be at risk; desired outcomes to keep contract; decision deadline.
2) Evidence collection: usage logs, recent support tickets, QBR slides, recent evals/quality checks.
3) Owner assignment: CSM (primary), SE (technical runbook), AE (commercial), Renewal Ops observer.
4) Initial score using Risk heatmap and record in renewal tracker row.

Playbook matrix (choose 1–2 plays based on root cause):
- Re-anchor value (product/usage):
  * Short PV sprint: 7–10 day engineering/SE mini-engagement that delivers a measurable business metric (e.g., latency drop, accuracy bump on key prompts).
  * Quick wins checklist: fine-tune prompts, caching adjustments, cost/latency config change; deliver before next check-in.
- Quality/regression fixes:
  * Hotfix lane: prioritize triaged bugs with SRE/serving-runtime; 48–72h SLAs for critical items.
  * Regression rollback: deploy prior model variant for affected routes with controlled monitoring.
- Commercial remediation:
  * Usage credit + PV recheck: conditional credit tied to a 30-day usage target.
  * Structured concession ladder: small commercial credits phase to larger only if technical fixes miss targets.
- Executive-sponsor play:
  * 30-minute sponsor alignment call (CS lead + AE + customer exec + our exec).
  * Outcome: commitment on 2 concrete next steps and a date for final renewal decision.
- Procurement/unblock play:
  * Legal/Proc template fast-track: AE + RevOps shepherd an accelerated signature pack for time-sensitive renewals.

Escalation matrix and criteria:
- Escalate to CS Director when risk score >= 19 or AE flags revenue > $100k ARR at risk.
- Escalate to VP Sales for enterprise renewals > $500k ARR or when commercial concessions exceed 10% of ARR.
- Exec sponsor handshake if customer requests executive-level intervention or if 2 successive PV attempts fail.
- Use these channels: #cs-lifeboat (Slack), renewal-ops@redwood.ai, Escalation doc (link in tracker).

Tracking & SLA: single source of truth columns to maintain (this also maps to QBR prep):
- CSM owner, AE owner, Renewal Ops observer
- Risk score (numeric) + band
- Root cause tag(s) (product, cost, people, legal)
- Current play(s) active and start date
- Next milestone date and owner
- Metrics: target metric, baseline, current value, delta
- Commercial offers (if any) and expiry date
- Outcome & final disposition (renewed, downgraded, churned)

Customer-facing templates (short):
- 1) 20-min intake invite (email)
Subject: Quick check-in on [Product] ahead of contract renewal
Hi [Name],
We want to make sure we address any concerns before your renewal decision. Can we do a 20-min check-in this week to align on priorities and share a short plan to demonstrate continued value?
Thanks,
[CSM]

- 2) 7-day PV offer (email)
Subject: 7-day value sprint: target [metric]
Hi [Name],
Per our conversation, we’re proposing a focused 7-day sprint to demonstrate X improvement on [metric]. Scope: [bullet 1], [bullet 2]. Success criteria: [metric target]. If we hit this, we’ll set a follow-up demo and propose a path forward.
Regards,
[SE] + [CSM]

Decision guide and 'win boundary' (what counts as a successful save):
- Minimum acceptable outcomes by day 14: either a) measurable lift in agreed metric that addresses the buyer's top concern (>= agreed threshold), or b) a signed commitment to a closed remediation cadence and an executive alignment date.
- If neither is met, prepare a controlled offboarding plan and handoff to customer success operations to minimize churn impact.

Post-mortem and learning loop (for every lifeboat):
- 10-day retrospective: 30–60 minute internal review capturing root cause, time-to-fix, what worked, what didn't, and a 1-paragraph TL;DR for execs.
- Update playbook: add one small, prescriptive change (e.g., new email template, new metric to capture) and push to the shared playbook repo.

Operational notes / Quick tips:
- Keep plays narrow. Do two things well instead of many things poorly.
- Avoid blanket concessions. Tie credits/offers to measurable milestones and expiry.
- Prefer technical remediation + PV over pure discounting when possible.
- For strategic accounts, pair a technical PV with an exec alignment to accelerate trust.

Appendix: recommended fields for the renewal tracker row (comma-separated description to paste into a sheet):
Customer,CSM,AE,Renewal Date,Risk Score,Risk Band,Root Cause Tags,Active Play(s),Play Start,Milestone 1 Date,Milestone 1 Owner,Baseline Metric,Target Metric,Current Metric,Commercial Offer,Offer Expiry,Escalation Level,Final Outcome,Notes

Quick references and owner contacts:
- Renewal Ops: renewal-ops@redwood.ai
- Escalation Slack: #cs-lifeboat
- Legal fast-track: legal-fasttrack@redwood.ai

This document is intentionally lightweight and designed to be copied into QBR templates and the renewal tracker sheet. Use iteratively and log every lifeboat to build a library of what saves work for different segments (SMB vs Mid-Market vs Enterprise).
